title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's mathematics. It is a typed Bourbaki internal circular, 'Tribu n° 66'. It records the congress decisions on two drafts for the Integration book: rédaction 446 (the second edition of Intégration, chap. V) and rédaction 447 (measures on Hausdorff spaces). The archival foliation '18' is in the lower left corner. The sheet happens to be filed among Grothendieck's crystal notes; the pages before and after concern Dieudonné-type data (ω, F, V) on S_zar versus S_cris, and descent of triangles.

Decisions on 446 (Integration V, second edition):
- The re-edition is adopted with enthusiasm. Paul-André Meyer and Adrien Douady are writing the final version.
- The notation \bar{μ}^* (essential upper integral) is replaced by μ°. In print this became μ•.
- 'tempérée' becomes 'modérée' (def. 2, p. 4), a pun on the politician Antoine Pinay, a 'modéré'. A summary (sorite) of moderate functions, sets and measures will be given.
- New terms: 'scalairement essentiellement intégrable' (resp. 'scalairement intégrable'), and 'μ-adéquate' in def. 1, p. 21, generalising the notion of the current edition.
- A proposal for fold-out sheets mapping the nested 'chapeaux' (hats/notations) and their domains of validity is rejected.

Decisions on 447 (measures on Hausdorff spaces):
- Bourbaki regrets not having restricted chapters III–IV to compact spaces and then passed directly to general Hausdorff spaces. This is called 'the triumphant resurrection of compactologies', but it is too late to rewrite III–IV.
- The material will form a separate chapter IX at the end of the book, with a Leitfaden showing its dependencies. This is the published Intégration chap. IX (1969), on measures on Hausdorff spaces, Radon measures and projective limits.
- Douady and Meyer will write the next version. Laurent Schwartz will supply a paper on Wiener–Lévy measure on C([0,1]).

There is no mathematical argument to reconstruct; it is editorial history of Bourbaki.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a Bourbaki Tribu (congress report) on the re-edition of Integration V and the genesis of chap. IX. It is mildly interesting archival history: it shows Grothendieck still held Bourbaki circulars, and it records the Douady/Meyer authorship and the 'compactologies' regret. Such material is known from the Bourbaki archives, and it contains no Grothendieck mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially accurate; 'ressurection' is the typist's spelling in the original.
This is a typed Bourbaki document, not a manuscript by Grothendieck; the '18' in the lower left is the archival foliation.
